minutes.headline: Selectmen recommended the marijuana dispensary bylaw, right-to-farm bylaw and FY14 budget amendments for Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: The Select Board reviewed warrant articles ahead of Town Meeting, hearing the planning board on the medical marijuana bylaw and the agricultural commission on right to farm. It recommended the FY14 budget amendments, discussed the land use director reorganization pending Town Counsel and a public hearing, abated an ambulance bill, backed the mosquito control assessment, and reviewed third quarter financials.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to recommend Town Meeting approval of the registered marijuana dispensary zoning bylaw, Article 27.
The Board voted to recommend the right to farm bylaw, Article 28, after the agricultural commission said it would show the moderator four wording corrections.
The Board voted to recommend Article 9, FY14 budget amendments that move surpluses from some lines to cover deficits in others, plus a free cash appropriation.
The land use director reorganization went to a public hearing set for next Tuesday, with the manager to add Sewer Commission and DPW coordination.
The Board abated an ambulance bill as documented and backed the mosquito control assessment by naming the Board of Health chair as designee.

why_it_matters: Articles 27, 28 and 9 will come before residents at Town Meeting, where the Board's recommendations are on record but the votes are residents' to take.
The Article 9 transfers and the unpaid prior-year police medical bill show how year-end deficits are covered from other lines and free cash, which are town funds drawn mostly from taxes.
The land use reorganization would change how zoning, building and related permitting staff are organized, so the coming hearing is the place to comment.
watch_next: Public hearing on the land use reorganization, set for next Tuesday.
The Monty Tech FY15 revised assessment and the manager's recommendation to reappropriate the savings to the schools, and the police injured-on-duty bill, due back next week.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main votes (Articles 27, 28, 9, the ambulance abatement and the mosquito control designee) and on most figures, apart from caption-garbled numbers and names. The main differences are the public hearing item (ours says a land use reorganization hearing next Tuesday; the official says Article 19 on 4/29/2014), the Article 9 "229 thousand" figure that the official minutes do not give, and the many official items our minutes do not cover.
